lines: They sold the house last spring
the ivy came down with the sign
I drove past just to see it
and kept the engine running
The kitchen clock still runs
on nobody's time now
the porch swing lost its chain
but I still hear it somehow
She kept the good plates hidden
for company that never came
the phone still has her numbers
and every name sounds the same
I kept the kitchen key
though no one's left to see
the yard has learned to grieve
and some part of me won't leave
The attic still smells like cedar
boxes nobody claimed
the stairs still creak at the landing
just like they never were named
I kept the kitchen key
though no one's left to see
the yard has learned to grieve
and some part of me won't leave
I'll keep the kitchen clock running
on nobody's time at all
I'll leave the porch light burning
and answer if it ever calls
Someone else mows the lawn now
the swing set's finally gone
but the kitchen clock keeps time
in a house that isn't mine
